dimensions.name: structural_integrity
findings: CRIT-004's passThreshold (structural_integrity, weight 0.2) encodes REQ-RL17's wiring requirement using ONLY PROP-RL-WIRE1's ast keyword-presence scan ('every Call to decide_promotion carries a realized_gate keyword argument'). It completely omits REQ-RL17's own second sentence (specs/behavioral-spec.md:286-290): 'the Phase-3 implementation review SHALL verify that the value bound to realized_gate= at each call site is genuinely sourced from the REQ-RL7-13 computation helper over the resolved ledger — never a hardcoded literal, stub dict, or constant that would satisfy the repo-scan's keyword-presence check while bypassing real data.' PROP-RL-WIRE1 as written in this contract is EXACTLY the keyword-presence check REQ-RL17 itself warns is satisfiable by a stub: an implementation that writes decide_promotion(..., realized_gate={'resolved': True, 'trend_blocks': False, 'realism_gap_blocks': False, ...}) as a hardcoded literal at all three promote_gate_run.py call sites (never calling compute_realized_gate at all) would pass PROP-RL-WIRE1's ast scan and satisfy CRIT-004 in full, while defeating the entire point of the feature (a candidate would always sail through the realized-ledger gate regardless of real ledger content). Neither CRIT-004's description nor its passThreshold names this anti-stub/genuine-sourcing check as a required pass condition anywhere in the contract, and there is no PROP-RL-* ID for it in verification-architecture.md's Proof Obligations table (it is inherently a judgment call, not an automatable pytest assertion) — meaning it can ONLY be carried into the contract as explicit prose, the same technique this contract already correctly uses elsewhere (CRIT-006's 'not merely claimed'/'evidence... not a prose claim' language for its own judgment-based live-tier checks). Because it is silently absent, the fresh-context Phase-3 adversary reading only this contract has no instruction to verify realized_gate's genuine provenance at each of the three call sites, so a stubbed/hardcoded implementation could pass Phase-3 review purely on WIRE1's automated scan. This is a real weakening of REQ-RL17 relative to the spec, not a missing test citation.

evidence.description: REQ-RL17's own text explicitly splits into two halves: (1) ast-scan keyword-presence (delegated to PROP-RL-WIRE1), and (2) Phase-3 review verifying the bound value is genuinely computed, not a stub/hardcoded literal — the contract only encodes half (1)
